---
title: "OpenCode login and model routes"
---

Connect OpenCode to an available model provider. This page was checked 2026-09-12. If the menus differ, follow the current [provider guide](https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/).

## Connect

1. From the selected lab directory, run `opencode`.
2. For OpenCode Zen, sign in at `opencode.ai/auth` and create an API key. Add billing details only if the current flow requires them.
3. In the TUI (terminal user interface), run `/connect`, choose **OpenCode Zen**, and paste the key into the documented prompt. Run `/models` and select an available model.
4. For OpenRouter or NVIDIA, get a key through the provider's official process. Then run `/connect`, choose the provider, enter the key in the documented prompt, and run `/models`.
5. Send a harmless orientation prompt and confirm the working directory before allowing edits.

You can also watch the [Zen](../media/videos/opencode-zen-api.mp4), [OpenRouter](../media/videos/opencode-openrouter-api.mp4), or [NVIDIA](../media/videos/opencode-nvidia-api.mp4) walkthrough. Screens may have changed.

Before the first prompt, check that the working directory contains only the workshop repository and fake data. Start with ordinary approval prompts. The labs introduce auto mode later.

::: {.callout-tip title="Workshop fallback if free credits run out"}
The Codespace already knows the workshop fallback provider and models. Get the temporary key from the facilitator through the announced secure channel, then set it in your current terminal:

```bash
export WORKSHOP_API_KEY="sk-diw-..."
```

Start OpenCode, run `/models`, and choose a model under **Workshop fallback**. You do not need to edit an OpenCode JSON file. The export lasts only for that terminal session; never paste the real key into chat, a README, or a commit.
:::

OpenCode Zen describes zero-retention/no-training defaults with named exceptions. Check its live [retention table](https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/). OpenRouter routes follow the terms of the selected provider and account.

::: {.callout-warning}
Never put an API key in a shell command, README, chat, issue, or commit. Prompts may be retained or used for model improvement, depending on the provider and account. Never enter restricted SOEP rows, unpublished findings, personal information, or participant material. Public data is not automatically approved for an external AI service.
:::

If authentication fails, stop and ask the facilitator. Do not expose a secret to make the demo work.
